creativeDirection: Daylight location photography in a real indoor pool, using one cast portrait anchored in a recognisable architectural place with a few small physical motifs from other sleeves folded into the same moment.
scene: An empty indoor swimming pool hall after hours, shot from the deck at eye level along one side of the pool. Cool blue tiled walls, pale concrete deck, lane ropes disappearing softly behind, and a few warm hanging bulbs over the near side create a crisp editorial atmosphere. The cast figure stands near the pool edge in the near-middle ground, with the room wrapping around her rather than a staged backdrop.

elements.element: the woman from reference image 1 standing by the pool in her white swim cap decorated with yellow daisies, facing the camera in the same close-portrait spirit
two small warm hanging bulbs suspended over the pool deck near the camera side
a soft monochrome tonal treatment in a brushed stainless wall panel and pale grey seating area that echoes the plain black-and-white studio restraint
a folded patterned fan resting on a plastic bench beside the pool
a dark crucifix necklace hanging from a metal hook with a towel nearby
a muted blush-pink accent in one section of painted wall
a hard black-and-white contrast note in the deck shadows and tile grout
clean white-and-charcoal tonal balance in the room

prompt: An empty indoor swimming pool hall after hours, viewed from the deck at eye level along one side of the pool, a real architectural interior with cool blue tiled walls, pale concrete, lane ropes, metal hooks, plastic benches, and a few warm hanging bulbs over the near side; the woman from reference image 1 stands near the pool edge in the near-middle ground at three-quarter length, facing the camera with the same poised expression, strong eyeliner, red lipstick, and white swim cap decorated with yellow daisies, lit by the room's own overhead pool lights and the warm bulbs so her face is crisp and clear; include two small glowing hanging bulbs from reference image 2 near the camera side, a folded patterned fan from reference image 5 resting on a bench, and a dark crucifix necklace from reference image 8 hanging from a metal hook beside a towel; let reference image 3 contribute plain monochrome restraint in a brushed steel panel and pale grey seating area, while reference images 4, 6, and 7 contribute only blush, contrast, and white-charcoal tonal balance; photographic realism, clean editorial location photography, sharp focus, no haze, no collage, no posters or pictures on surfaces; off-centre environmental portrait with the subject on one side and pool space opening beside her, faces properly lit, crisp small-scale readability; palette of cool blue, purple-blue, white, yellow, warm amber, blush pink, and charcoal, with a quiet poised slightly uncanny mood. Reference map for people (the album images are attached in this numbered order): reference image 1 shows one woman in close-up wearing a floral swim cap. Copy each of these faces directly from that numbered reference image - same face, bone structure, hair, expression, and styling - rather than drawing a new person from the description. Nobody from reference images 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8 appears in the picture: use those images only for colour, setting, and objects, and add no figures, faces, or silhouettes from them. Hard constraints (override any conflicting source material): Create a single cohesive 16:9 image, not a grid, contact sheet, row of covers, or collage of separate panels. Do not reproduce the album sleeves as framed thumbnails, posters, record covers, or pictures on a screen, monitor, or television. A sleeve's abstract graphics, shapes, patterns, and colours may be painted onto the walls, doors, floor, or objects of the place as part of its decoration, without any lettering. Show no sleeve's faces, heads, or figures as a picture, mural, display, sign, relief, or silhouette anywhere; transform the sleeves' non-text visual motifs into one original composition. Include no readable text or lettering of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, code, glyphs, captions, titles, logos, watermarks, labels, or signage. Feature only adults and avoid gore, wounds, body horror, medical or anatomical imagery, blank or milky eyes, nudity, sexual content, weapons, and hate symbols; reinterpret any sensitive source motif abstractly. When a source includes a person, closely match their visible appearance and likeness to the reference image, preserving recognisable facial features, hair, skin tone, clothing, and styling, and their apparent age: every person is shown as the adult they are on the sleeve, never younger, smoothed, or more boyish or girlish. Keep each reference person in the pose, expression, and gaze the sleeve shows, and keep every identifiable face sharp, lit, unobscured, and in focus: no motion blur, long-exposure smearing, steam, fog, shadow, crowding, or shallow depth of field over a reference person's face. Expose the image cleanly whatever the light: every person's face well lit and readable, shadows that hold detail, and clear colour, with no murky underexposure, crushed blacks, heavy film grain, digital noise, or dust-and-scratches texture. Add no incidental plants: no flowers, potted plants, planters, climbing vines, ivy, hanging foliage, hedges, lawns, flower beds, or greenery framing the edges or carpeting the floor, unless the description above explicitly asks for that plant as part of a source motif or the year treatment. Dress the scene with the materials of the place itself - stone, metal, concrete, wood, fabric, glass, water, equipment - rather than vegetation. Everyone in the picture is photographed in the same place, at the same moment, under the same light as the rest of the scene, in full colour and with the same lens and grain: do not carry over a sleeve's own backdrop, studio lighting, backlit flare, monochrome, colour cast, or print texture onto the person. Each person stands inside the scene at the scale of the space around them, never as an oversized cropped head or bust looming at the edge of the frame over a distant scene, and never washed in red, blue, or other coloured light. Depict each identifiable reference person only once in the entire composition; do not repeat or clone them as another figure, reflection, mirror portrait, poster, billboard, screen, photograph, painting, silhouette, or background face. The only exception is repetition visibly intrinsic to one source cover: keep that repetition within that single source motif and do not echo the person elsewhere. The only people anywhere in the image are the reference people named in the reference map, and of those only the ones whose faces are clearly visible in their reference. Add no one else: no extra band members, musicians, staff, bystanders, passers-by, crowd, audience, background or out-of-focus figures, and no hands, arms, legs, or shadows of unseen people. Never complete a person who is hidden, cropped, turned away, blurred, or only partly visible in a reference with an invented face or body - leave that person out entirely. Photograph the reference people from roughly eye level, at three-quarter length or closer, in the near or middle ground, so each of their faces is large, sharp, and clearly recognisable in the final frame: never from directly above, and never as small distant figures.
